clue.text: Hastened to hide flag seized in transit

indicators.note: to hide something is to cover it, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: hied is an old word meaning hastened or hurried
a jack is a ship's flag, as in the Union Jack

explanation.surface: Someone rushed to conceal a banner that was confiscated during a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle hijacked has been taken over by force while on its route.

clue.text: Striking workers heading off home

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farm hands

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of home is removed

explanation.surface: Workers on strike leave and set off for home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' suggests industrial action alongside 'workers', but it means good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: A striking face is a good-looking, attractive one.

clue.text: He saw ladder about to be moved up into position

indicators.note: into means the turned piece goes inside the word for position

parts.note: a job is a position or post

indicators.note: moved up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A man spotted a ladder about to be raised into place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be moved up' turns CA into AC, which goes into JOB. In Genesis, Jacob dreamt of a ladder to heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Jacob dreamt of a ladder reaching to heaven with angels on it.

clue.text: What divers may do, itching to make the grade

definitions.meaning: a diver surfacing to relieve an itch would rise to the surface to scratch

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means reaching an acceptable standard; literally, divers surfacing to scratch an itch.

clue.text: Justify being newly decorated?

definitions.meaning: to give reasons for or account for something
something just decorated is no longer plain, so it is formerly plain

explanation.definitionFit: To account for or make clear one's actions is to justify them; also read as former plainness.

clue.text: More work -— work I put into out-tray regularly

indicators.note: put into tells us the next pieces go inside the letters picked from the tray
regularly means taking every other letter of the word out-tray

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
taken as written

explanation.surface: An overloaded office worker sighs at yet more paperwork landing in the out-tray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' at the start hides its capital: it is Sir Thomas More, whose most famous work is the definition, not a call for extra work. 'regularly' picks UTA from out-tray.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More, the Tudor statesman, wrote the book of that title describing an ideal society.

clue.text: Modernist novel from T S Eliot, though he needed translating

indicators.note: needed translating means these letters must be converted into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A modernist novel came out of T S Eliot, though he needed a translator.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf's 1927 book is a landmark of modernist fiction.

clue.text: Wading bird seen amazingly in a poplar, eh?

indicators.note: amazingly suggests the letters are thrown into surprising disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to see a wading bird perched in a poplar tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A phalarope is a small wading bird of the sandpiper family.

clue.text: United recovered after surrendering lead

indicators.note: surrendering lead means the word for recovered loses its first letter

parts.note: rallied means recovered, as a team or patient does

explanation.surface: Manchester United came back after giving up a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture of United losing a lead misleads: United is the definition, meaning joined in alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Allied nations are joined together in an alliance, so they are united.

clue.text: Strip club is over the way

indicators.note: is over in a down clue places the first word above the second

parts.note: a dive is a seedy club or bar
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A strip club stands just across the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to strip someone of clothing, rights or possessions.

clue.text: Having a little screen, I came for digital TV system

indicators.note: having a little of these words means holding a short run of their letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone reports that since getting a small screen, they've been watching digital TV.
explanation.definitionFit: This acronym names the digital stereo sound standard once used by British television broadcasts.

clue.text: Game leader of brigade brought in to decorate everybody

indicators.note: brought in says the picked letter is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: to paint is to decorate a room
all means everybody

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of brigade

explanation.surface: A fire brigade chief is called in to help redecorate for the whole team.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sport in which players shoot each other with pellets of dye.

clue.text: Master of one vessel worried about another

parts.note: a sub, or submarine, is a vessel
another vessel: a jug holds liquid
ate, as in what's eating you, means worried

explanation.surface: A ship's captain frets about a second ship nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' looks like a ship's captain in this seafaring picture, but it is a verb meaning to conquer; 'another' points back to vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a people is to conquer or overcome them, bringing them under control.

clue.text: Clear answer given in Gaelic

indicators.note: given in shows one letter being placed inside a word

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland

explanation.surface: A straightforward reply is spoken in the Gaelic tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a board or a record is to wipe it, removing what was written.

clue.text: Muddle can reveal where Tommy Tucker was seen

parts.note: a mess is a muddle
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A confusing nursery rhyme makes you wonder where little Tommy Tucker was spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Tucker is the nursery-rhyme boy, but here a Tommy is a British soldier and tucker is food: a soldier's food is seen in his metal mess tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier, nicknamed a Tommy, eats his rations or grub from his metal dish in the field.

clue.text: Devil-may-care or punch-drunk?

definitions.meaning: dazed as if from repeated blows, read as happy from slaps

explanation.definitionFit: Carefree casualness is one sense; dazed by hitting is the literal reading of the hyphenated word.

clue.text: Specially adapt as follower of tinker

definitions.meaning: to fit or customise something for a particular purpose
in the rhyme Tinker, ..., Soldier, Sailor, the second trade comes straight after tinker

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to customise clothes or plans; the other is the counting rhyme's second occupation.

clue.text: Actual bore said by some to be obliging

definitions.text: said by some to be obliging

parts.note: very can mean actual, as in the very man
a well is a bore, a hole drilled for water

explanation.surface: A genuine bore is reported to be very helpful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' suggests a dull person, but it is a borehole. The phrase is what an obliging person says on agreeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the phrase signals agreement, so it is what accommodating people say.

clue.text: Fastener needs new washer

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of washer are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A fitting needs a fresh washer to stay tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washer' looks like part of the plumbing picture, but it is the fodder for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope or cable used to moor or tow ships, so it fastens them.

clue.text: Touching cord? It's instinctive

parts.note: re means about or concerning, touching on
a flex is an electrical cord

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a cord and is told the response is automatic.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex reaction is automatic and involuntary, done without conscious thought.

clue.text: Win? In pain, I've failed

indicators.note: In tells us one piece sits inside another

parts.note: an ache is a pain

indicators.note: failed suggests the letters of I've have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A struggling competitor asks whether they won while hurting from a failed attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Win?' reads as a question about a contest, but it is the definition, a verb; 'failed' gives IEV from I've, and 'In' puts it inside the pain word.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve a goal is to gain or attain it, much as to win it.

clue.text: Vigorous supporter's bitter about job

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: bitter is a type of ale, an English beer
a post is a job

explanation.surface: An eager fan is resentful about their employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' looks like a resentful mood but is the English beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a passionate advocate for a cause, like one of Christ's first followers.

clue.text: Game that's even (nothing in it)

indicators.note: in it tells us the letter for nothing goes inside the word for even

parts.note: quits means even, all square
O stands for nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A game finishes level, with a nil score inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoits is a game of throwing rings over a peg.

clue.text: Effusive person's no good as escort

indicators.note: no here means having none of the following letter, so it is removed

parts.note: a gusher is someone who talks effusively

explanation.surface: A gushing person is no use as someone's companion for the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows people to their seats, escorting them at a wedding or theatre.

clue.text: Following strawberry dish writer gets rash

indicators.note: following means the writer's name comes after the dish in the answer

parts.note: a fool is a dessert of fruit and cream, such as a strawberry fool
Thomas Hardy was an English novelist

explanation.surface: After eating a strawberry pudding, an author breaks out in a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint after the dessert, but it is the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolhardy and rash both mean recklessly bold, acting without thought for danger.

clue.text: Bears, losing billions, get damages

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away from the word for bears

parts.note: bruin is an old name for a bear

explanation.surface: A stock market falling on the bears loses billions in damages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damages' looks like a noun of compensation but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to damage it severely, wrecking it.

clue.text: Profession of one in theatre, showing anxiety

parts.note: a profession here is a declaration, so the statement I'M is how someone professes
a patient is someone in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: Someone states their job in the theatre while visibly nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Profession' looks like a career, but it means a declaration: a person on the operating table professes I'M PATIENT, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless and eager for things to happen is fretful, unable to wait calmly.

clue.text: Almost all of team linked to Sheffield Wed?

indicators.note: almost all of a word means dropping its final letter

parts.note: Sheffield United is a football club in the English city of Sheffield

explanation.surface: Most of a football side has ties to Sheffield Wednesday, the city's other club.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheffield United and Sheffield Wednesday are rival football clubs; 'Wed' looks like the club but is the definition, to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed is to marry, and marriage joins two people together as one.

clue.text: One cuts article after audible expression of exasperation

indicators.note: after means the article comes later in the answer
audible tells us the letters are spelt as the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: a sigh is a sound of weariness or exasperation
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone cuts out a newspaper article after giving a weary sigh.
explanation.definitionFit: A scythe is a long-bladed tool for cutting grass or corn, so it is one that cuts.

clue.text: Poem shortened in actual change for the worse

indicators.note: in places the shortened poem inside another word

parts.note: real means actual

indicators.note: shortened means the last letter of the word for poem is cut

parts.note: a verse is a poem

explanation.surface: A poem gets cut down, actually a worse result than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'actual' looks like an adverbial filler in the surface but supplies a synonym; 'shortened' drops the poem's final letter, giving VERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal of fortune is a setback, a turn of events for the worse.
